questions.q: Why is migrating from a Zebra to a BV420D low-risk for the customer?
o: ZPL II emulation means existing label templates and BarTender workflow carry across
Zebra and Toshiba use identical part numbers
questions.e: ZPL II emulation plus the same BarTender design workflow makes it a driver reinstall and config step, not a workflow rebuild.

questions.q: The Zebra ZD421 has more standard memory than the BV420D. When does that actually matter?
o: Only for very large on-device font libraries or extensive stored label formats
questions.e: The extra memory only matters for large Unicode font sets or many stored formats; standard retail, logistics and healthcare labelling never approaches the BV420D's limits.

questions.q: What is the Bixolon XD5-40's role in the 'Kill the Zebra' strategy?
o: The primary label-printer replacement for the Zebra ZD421 — the default on all displacement and new business
A scanner replacement for the Zebra DS9308
A handheld computer replacing the Zebra TC52
A mobile printer with no displacement role
questions.e: Bixolon is IOR's primary Zebra label-printer replacement; the XD5-40 is the default quote for the ZD421 installed base. Toshiba is the on-request secondary.

questions.q: A customer has Zebra TC52 handhelds. What is the IOR replacement?
questions.e: The mid-tier TC52/57/58 family maps to the Urovo DT50.

questions.q: What is the BV420D's max direct-thermal print speed at 203 dpi?
questions.e: The BV420D runs 7 ips at 203 dpi versus the Zebra ZD421's 6 ips — about 17% faster.

questions.q: Which Epson printer is purpose-built for tablet/cloud POS, with USB-C power delivery and integrated Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in a compact cube?
questions.e: The TM-m30III is the mPOS unit: USB-C PD to power a tablet, integrated Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, tiny footprint, ePOS-Print for cloud apps.

questions.q: When does Toshiba get quoted on a Zebra label-printer replacement?
o: Only when the customer specifically requests Toshiba, or an existing Toshiba estate / service-network requirement makes it the better fit
questions.e: Bixolon is the primary and the default quote on all displacement and new business. Toshiba is the on-request secondary — customer asks for it, or a Toshiba estate / service-network requirement is in scope.

questions.q: What Android version and upgrade path do the lead Urovo models (e.g. RT40S) ship with?
questions.e: RT40S ships on Android 13 with GMS/AER and a stated path to Android 17 — important for 4–5 year deployments.

questions.scenario: A hospital uses Zebra ZD510 wristband printers and ZQ610 mobile printers on the wards.
questions.q: What's the right approach before you quote?
o: Map ZD510 to the Bixolon healthcare equivalent (confirm exact model with product team) and ZQ610 to the Urovo SP319/SP409, but pre-qualify the ZPL/SDK requirement first
Quote both immediately as straight drop-ins
Replace the wristband printer with a Datalogic scanner
questions.e: The ZD510 maps to a Bixolon healthcare equivalent that must be confirmed with the product team, and the ZQ610 maps to a Urovo mobile printer where ZPL needs SDK work — both carry caveats to resolve before quoting.
